{{infobox weapon | title = Staff of Protection | description = For a slight blood offering it will protect the caster in a magical shell. | id = StaffShield | type = Blood magic | source = Galdr table | weight = 0.3 | crafting level = 1 | repair level = 1 | materials 1 = * [[Yggdrasil Wood]] x20 * [[Blood Clot]] x4 * [[Refined Eitr]] x16 | materials 2 = * [[Yggdrasil Wood]] x10 * [[Blood Clot]] x2 * [[Refined Eitr]] x8 | materials 3 = * [[Yggdrasil Wood]] x20 * [[Blood Clot]] x4 * [[Refined Eitr]] x16 | eitr = 60 | block armor = 48 | block force = 20 | block force per level = 5 | parry bonus = 2 | movement speed = -5% | durability = 200 | wielding = Two-handed |health = 40% |adrenaline = 6 }} The '''Staff of Protection''' is one of four [[Magic]] weapons introduced in the [[Mistlands]] update. Its primary use creates a protective barrier around the caster, as well as other players and tamed creatures next to the user. In addition to requiring 60 [[Eitr]] to be cast, the caster will lose up to 40% of their current [[Health]] (''not'' their maximum health). Like the other magic weapons, it has no secondary ability. The amount of damage absorbed by the barrier is highly dependent on the caster's [[Blood magic]] skill level: While the base damage absorption (at level 0) is 200, it increases by 5 per level up to a maximum of 700 damage (at level 100). Similarly, how much health is drained upon casting is also affected by the caster's blood magic level, as is how much eitr is required: at level 100, both will be reduced by 1/3. == Upgrade information ==

Beyond quality 4, the Staff of Protection can be upgraded further at the [[Forge of Potential]] with a [[Black Marble Battle Idol]]. == Notes == * The barrier does not inherit any resistances, immunities or armor values of the target it is applied to, thus it is raw HP with a damage gate to prevent overflow into the affected target's health (this includes stagger). Notably, this means that monster damage which is harmless to the player like Chop and Pickaxe can suddenly become a major threat to the barrier, causing it to be destroyed quicker than expected. * Recasting the Staff of Protection on a target with a barrier already active will reset the time limit of their barrier, but will ''not'' reset their barrier's absorption amount. Thus, a barrier that has already been substantially weakened will have its duration extended, but will also remain just as weak after a recast. ** When trying to maintain one or more barriers during heavy fighting, casters should prioritize recasting on targets whose barriers have already broken, as recasting on targets with active but damaged barriers will merely be a waste of eitr and health. * A player with an active barrier can always succeed in parrying an attack, regardless of their weapon, max hp, or stagger limit, even if the attack results in the barrier being broken. ** This functionally means the player can always parry at least one attack per cast - which can make even 2-star late-game enemies parryable, thus opening them to additional damage. {{Weapons}} [[ru:Посох защиты]]

Bow (4 seconds) | veryweak = | weak = Blunt, Fire | resistant = Pierce, Frost | veryresistant = | immune = Poison | stagger = 50%}} }} The '''Dead Raiser''' is one of the four [[Mistlands]] [[Magic]] weapons. When cast, a '''Skelett''' (a tamed [[Skeleton]]) spawns near the caster. The skelett will follow its summoner and attacks any non-tame creature that comes close, except for neutral [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. They are much stronger than normal Skeletons, even compared to [[Creature Level|2-star]] variants. In addition to requiring up to 100 [[Eitr]] to be cast, the caster will lose up to 40% of their current [[Health]] (''not'' their maximum health). Like the other magic weapons, it has no secondary ability. Similarly, how much health is drained upon casting is also affected by the caster's [[Blood magic]] level, as is how much eitr is required: at level 100, both will be reduced by 1/3. ==Skelett== '''Skeletts''' are [[Creatures]] summoned by players using the [[Dead Raiser]]. As summons, they fight on behalf of nearby players, attacking any nearby hostile creatures. Otherwise, they look and behave similar to [[Skeleton]]s, except for being purple in color. Skeletts come in two variants: A melee-oriented type with sword and (optionally) shield, and an archer type with a bow and arrows. The amount of damage dealt by its summons is highly dependent on the caster's [[Blood magic]] skill level: each Skelett's damage increases by 2% per level up to a maximum of +200% (x3) of their base values (at level 100). Their [[Health]] is not affected by skill level. Summoned skeletts will randomly spawn with a [[Bronze Sword]] (80% chance) or a wooden [[Bows|bow]] (20% chance); if the skelett has a sword, it may also spawn with a [[Wood Shield]] or a [[Bronze Buckler]] (25% chance each). Depending on the location, it may be advantageous to re-summon for melee- or archery-specific Skeletons. The Dead Raiser has a limit to how many summons it can control at once, which depends on its quality; if a player casts the Dead Raiser when they already have summoned the maximum number of skeletts, their oldest skelett will be killed off and a new one will be summoned. == Upgrade information == {| class="wikitable" !Quality !1 !2 !3 !4 |- !Maximum Skeletons Controllable |1 |2 |3 |4 |- !Durability |200 |250 |300 |350 |- !Crafting |10 [[Bone Fragments]]

8 [[Skeleton Trophy]] {{Upgrade station row|Galdr table|4|colspan=1}} |} Beyond quality 4, the Dead Raiser can be upgraded further at the [[Forge of Potential]] with a [[Black Marble Battle Idol]]. == Notes == * The Dead Raiser glows faintly purple-pink at all times. It is very dim compared to most proper light sources, but can provide a small amount of light in the dark. ** The glow effect also makes players slightly easier to detect while [[Sneak_(Skill)|sneaking]], increasing the visibility of its holder by approximately 10%. * As of the Mistlands update, no single [[Food]] item grants sufficient Eitr for players with low skill at Blood magic to use the Dead Raiser: Such players must consume at least two Eitr-focused foods to use it, leaving them with a lower maximum potential health pool. ** [[Blood magic]] level 47 is currently the minimum skill level at which a single food item ([[Seeker Aspic]]) will allow a player to cast the Dead Raiser. ** The high eitr requirement can be mitigated somewhat: Casters only need sufficient Eitr at the time of casting, not afterward. Therefore, players are somewhat free to eat different foods (either after waiting or through use of [[Bukeperries]]) after using the Dead Raiser, especially if they plan on keeping their Skeletts protected through use of e.g. the [[Staff of Protection]]. However, should one of their Skeletts die, they will become unable to summon any more until they once again have the required amount of eitr. * As of the Ashlands update, the best [[Food]] item for Eitr is [[Marinated Greens]], which still does not provide enough Eitr alone to use Dead Raiser until players have raised their [[Blood magic]] somewhat. ** Players who wish to use Dead Raiser with low Blood Magic can pair one Eitr food with [[Ashlands Gourmet Bowl]] or [[Mushrooms Galore á la Mistlands]] to somewhat mitigate the loss of health or stamina inherent to pairing two Eitr-specific foods. * Skeletts cannot swim or drown, and will instead walk on the seafloor. * Skeletts are considered ''tameable'' mobs, but are also ''always'' tame. This means that they can be pet like other tameable mobs. Additionally, like all tamed mobs, players are only able to ''damage'' them either by using the [[Butcher Knife]] or by enabling friendly fire mode. If the [[Dead Raiser]] is used by the player after the maximum number of Skeletts have been summoned, the oldest Skelett will be ''killed'' off and replaced with a new one. ** Killing a summoned Skelett before exceeding the maximum frees up one of the summoner's summon slots. They can then use the Dead Raiser to re-summon a new Skelett. This can be done on purpose to obtain the desired Skelett variants, or just to quickly get new ones with full health. * Skeletts are able to be shielded with a [[Staff of Protection]] in the same way that players can be. * It's easy to loose your Skeletons while sprinting for extended periods of time but as long as no portal is involved, they will eventually catch up. ==List of names== Skeletts always spawn with one of 99 possible names. They can also be re-named by players. Each name has a 1 in 101 chance of being selected, except for two names which are twice as likely. {{Collapsible|Click to show/hide|| {{cols|3| * Agda * Agnhild * Åke* * Alrik * Alvar * Arn * Arne * Åsa * Åse * Ask * Astrid * Birger * Björn * Bothild * Botvid * Brynhilda * Dagmar * Disa * Egil * Einar * Eivor * Embla * Erik * Fjalar * Fjolnir * Folke * Freydis * Frida * Gauti * Gefjon * Gerda * Gertrud * Gislaug * Gloin * Gorm * Grim * Gudrun * Gunhild * Gunvor * Gyda * Hakon * Halfdan* * Hallbjörn * Harald * Helga * Herja * Hervor * Hilda * Hjalmar * Hjördis * Holmfridur * Hunvor * Inga * Ingeborg * Jörgen * Karsten * Kata * Kjettil * Knut * Lars * Leif * Liv * Magnus * Nefja * Olaf * Ragnar * Ragnhild * Runa * Rune * Saxa * Signe * Sigrid * Sigrun * Skarpe * Skuli * Snari * Sten * Sune * Sveid * Sven * Thora * Thorbjörn * Thorleif * Tjarve * Toke * Torstein * Trygve * Turid * Tyra * Udd * Ulf * Ulfhild * Unna * Vedis * Verun * Vidar * Your best pal * Yrr * Yrsa }} * These names are twice as likely to appear. }}

[[Mörkhalla]] | usage = Crafting }} }} |Creatures| {{InfoboxTabber |Bear| {{infobox creature | image 0star = Bear.png | image 1star = | image 2star = | trophy = | id = Bjorn_spiritcaller | location = | drops = | health 0star = 1500 | damage 0star = * Bite: 100 Pierce * Claws: 90 Slash, 40 Chop * Slam: 100 Blunt, 40 Chop, 40 Pickaxe * Swipe combo, right: 50 Slash, 40 Chop * Swipe left: 25 Slash, 40 Chop | health 1star = | damage 1star = | health 2star = | damage 2star = | abilities = * Bite (4 seconds) * Claws (4 seconds) * Slam (12 seconds) * Swipe combo, right (4 seconds each for 2 variants) * Swipe left (4 seconds) | weak = Fire | resistant = Pierce, Blunt, Frost | immune = Spirit |stagger=30% |faction=Players }} |Moose| {{infobox creature | image 0star = Moose.png | image 1star = | image 2star = | trophy = | id = Moose_spiritcaller | location = | drops = | health 0star = 1100 | damage 0star = * Hooves: 150 Blunt * Horns: 160 Slash * Sweep: 145 Slash | health 1star = | damage 1star = | health 2star = | damage 2star = | abilities = * Hooves (4 seconds) * Horns (4 seconds) * Sweep (4 seconds) | weak = Fire | resistant = Slash, Blunt, Frost | immune = Spirit |stagger=30% |faction=Players }} |Wolf| {{infobox creature | image 0star = Wolf.png | image 1star = | image 2star = | trophy = | id = Wolf_spiritcaller | location = | drops = | health 0star = 800 | damage 0star = 140 Slash | health 1star = | damage 1star = | health 2star = | damage 2star = | abilities = Attack (5s each for 3 variants) | immune = Spirit |stagger=50% |faction=Players }} |Boar| {{infobox creature | image 0star = Boar.png | image 1star = | image 2star = | trophy = | id = Boar_spiritcaller | location = | drops = | health 0star = 1000 | damage 0star = 100 Blunt | health 1star = | damage 1star = | health 2star = | damage 2star = | abilities = Attack (5s) | immune = Spirit |stagger=50% |faction=Players }} }} }} '''Spirit Caller''' is a [[Deep North]] [[Blood magic]] summoning staff. The Spirit Caller can summon Spirit versions of [[Bear]], [[Moose]], [[Wolf]] and [[Boar]]. These creatures have increased Health and damage compared to their wild counterparts. They have a transparent violet hue. The maximum number of summons for each creature type is equal to the Spirit Caller's level: one of each type at level 1, two of each at level 2, and so on. On each cast, the type of the next creature summoned is chosen randomly; if that type has already reached its maximum, the cast fails. As a result, it can take a large number of casts to reach the maximum for all four types. Summoned creatures follow the player who summoned them. A summon disappears if it is more than 150 meters from that player, or 120 seconds after that player has left the game. Each cast costs 100 [[Eitr]] and 40% [[Health]]. While wielded, the staff reduces movement speed by 5%. It cannot be crafted directly, instead the player must craft the corresponding '''Cast: Spirit Caller''' at a level 3 [[Galdr Table]] and harden it in a [[Frost Foundry]], which takes 50 seconds. It is upgraded at the [[Galdr Table]], from level 4 for quality 2 up to level 6 for quality 4. The [[Forge of Potential]] upgrade for this staff uses a [[Bloodgold Battle Idol]]. ==Mould== '''Mould: Spirit Caller''' can be found: * By destroying trash piles in [[Winding Tunnels]]. * In chests buried at [[Memorial Site]]s. * By destroying weapon stands on the last floor of [[Mörkhalla]]. == Upgrade information == {| class="wikitable" !Quality !1 !2 !3 !4 !
